name: United States (4.0 GPA)
notes: There is NO single official US 4.0 scale — the College Board says schools calculate GPA differently. Ship PRESETS, never one hard-coded formula. max_points 5.0 is the weighted ceiling; unweighted ceiling is 4.0.

presets.label: College Board reference (whole letters, no plus/minus)
presets.note: Official reference table; many high schools use this.

presets.label: Plus/minus — tenths (3.7 / 3.3 / 2.7 series)
presets.note: Most common mapping across university registrars (Mizzou, UCLA Extension, IU).

presets.label: Plus/minus — thirds (3.67 / 3.33 / 2.67 series)
presets.note: Used by some schools (e.g. University of Toledo).

presets.label: A+ = 4.33 variant
presets.note: Arizona State registrar; LSAC transcript standardization.

retake_note: No national rule. 'Replace' keeps only the latest attempt; 'average' includes all attempts (UMKC policy since 1985).

sources.label: College Board BigFuture — how to calculate GPA (4.0 scale)
University of Missouri Academic Catalog — grades
UCLA Extension — credit grading (+0.3/-0.3, except A+)
UMKC — repeated courses included in GPA since 1985

traps: There is NO single official US 4.0 scale — never hard-code one formula.
GPA ÷ 4 × 100 is used by NO school — any %↔GPA conversion is estimate-only.
Weighted bumps (+0.5 honors / +1.0 AP-IB) are district conventions, not national policy — user-adjustable.
unverified: Any national US %↔letter table (does not exist; school-specific).
Weighted-GPA bumps as official policy (conventions only; vary by district).
US retake specifics as a national rule (both models documented at school level).
'D earns credit' universality (CB table implies; some schools require C).
weighted_note: Conventions only — vary by district. Often no bonus on D/F. User may set their own bumps.
